thread:
eli: Heads-up — customer 'GammaHealth' opened an escalation: intermittent 401s after yesterday's key rotation. They see failures from a subset of requests, intermittent across regions. Attached sample request ids below.

maya: Can you paste the request IDs + an example curl that hits our API so we can repro? Also need the org id they were calling with.

eli: Request IDs: rid=01F7X2Q9A1, rid=01F7X2Q9B2. Customer says they call with header x-org-id: org_gh_123 and Authorization: Bearer <service_key_redacted>. Saw errors around 15:03 UTC.

jordan: quick repro attempt — i can try this locally but can you confirm the exact curl they used? assuming endpoint is https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate, example I ran:

```bash
curl -v \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer svc_XXXXxxYY' \
  -H 'x-org-id: org_gh_123' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
```

eli: that's basically it. Customer also uses a proxy (internal CDN) that rewrites some headers. They said when bypassing the proxy the 401s stop.

support-bot: auth-service log snippet for rid=01F7X2Q9A1: 
  timestamp=2026-03-12T15:03:02Z level=warn component=auth msg="signature mismatch" expected_org=org_gh_456 token_org_claim=org_gh_123 request_header_x_org=org_gh_123 auth_result=403

alex: hmm — log shows token org claim=org_gh_123 but expected_org=org_gh_456. That suggests routing looked up the wrong project config for that request (expected_org), likely due to header rewriting or credential shadowing where the token belongs to one project but the request was routed to a different tenant.

maya: checklist for repro + debug bundle we need from customer: 
- full curl -v output (including raw request/response headers)
- one failing request id (we have two) and one successful request id for contrast
- the exact Authorization header (if they can't paste full key, paste the first 8 chars)
- timestamp window (15:00-15:10 UTC)
- proxy/CDN config if possible (does it rewrite x-org-id?)
- whether they rotate keys via our UI or via API (we've seen differences)

jordan: also ask them to run a curl that forces the token to be used against the same backend, e.g.:

```bash
curl -v \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer svc_XXXXxxYY' \
  -H 'x-org-id: org_gh_123' \
  -H 'x-forwarded-host: api.redwood.ai' \
  'https://us-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
```

eli: i decoded a tiny part of the token header they sent (they redacted it but gave the jwt payload b64): payload -> {sub: 'svc_gh_789', org: 'org_gh_123', scope: 'service'} — matches their claim. So token looks valid. The auth service decision to expect org_gh_456 is the mismatch.

alex: possible causes: 
- proxy rewrites x-org-id to a default org before routing decision (so auth lookup uses default org config)
- stale routing table on edge node (rare but seen after config push)
- customer accidentally used a service key tied to another internal project but set x-org-id to current one (token/project shadowing)

maya: immediate ask to the customer — please run the following and paste output:

```bash
curl -v \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <their_full_key_here_or_first8chars>' \
  -H 'x-org-id: org_gh_123' \
  -H 'x-request-id: test-rid-123' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
```

and include the server response headers and the exact value of x-request-id.

eli: I'll open an internal ticket for infra to pull auth/routing logs for the two rids across the ingress fleet (time window 2026-03-12T15:00:00Z to 2026-03-12T15:10:00Z).

jordan: if they can't share full key, ask them to generate a short-lived 1min test key and run the repro with that. That eliminates concerns about redacting.

support-bot: next steps checklist created: ticket #INC-4721 assigned to @jordan, requesting ingress routing dump + auth-decision traces for rid=01F7X2Q9A1,01F7X2Q9B2.

sre-oncall: pinging infra — i've kicked a trace job against the edge nodes for that window and pinned to us-west. link: https://internal.redwood/trace/INC-4721 (internal).

eli: thanks. i'll follow up with customer to get curl -v + proxy config. once we have raw headers + one good vs bad rid we can close the loop. :thumbsup:

maya: assigning follow-up to @jordan and @eli. leaving thread open for debug bundle.

jordan: quick note for repro: sometimes signature mismatch logs occur when the x-org-id header is missing and the router falls back to org derived from hostname mapping. if customer uses hostname aliasing via CDN make sure the alias maps to the expected org.

eli: copying customer support message sent to GammaHealth: "Hi — thanks, we've opened INC-4721 and need the exact curl -v output and one failing request-id. Once we have that we can pull auth traces and confirm if header rewriting or routing is to blame."

sre-oncall: marking this incident informational for now, will escalate to P2 if more users affected.

maya: thanks team — will update after customer shares the curl output.
